segments.text: D D L: how we create, change and remove the structure of a database.
SQL is one language with four sub-languages, grouped by what each statement acts on.
D D L, the data definition language, defines the structure: tables, columns and constraints. D M L reads and changes the rows inside them.
D C L controls permissions, and T C L decides when changes become permanent.
CREATE TABLE builds a new table. Each column gets a name, a data type and, if needed, its constraints.
Varchar two of sixty holds text of up to sixty characters. NUMBER takes the number of digits, and optionally how many of them are decimals.
CHAR is for fixed-length codes, and DATE stores a date, with the time too.
For an auto-numbered key, Oracle uses generated always as identity. There is no auto increment.
Constraints are the rules every row must respect. An inline constraint is written right next to its column: not null, or a check on the shirt number.
An out-of-line constraint comes after the last column. It can cover several columns, like the unique pair of team and shirt.
Give your constraints names: error messages then show them.
A foreign key can only reference a table that already exists. Create player before team, and Oracle stops you.
O R A zero zero nine four two: table or view does not exist.
So create the parent first, then the child. Dropping goes the other way: children first.
ALTER TABLE changes a table that already holds data. It is like renovating a house with people living in it.
ADD builds a new room. The two members have no email yet, so it is NULL, and the fee takes its default, twenty.
MODIFY enlarges one: the name can now hold eighty characters. RENAME COLUMN relabels a door.
And DROP COLUMN knocks a wall down. Through every change, the furniture, the rows, stays.
In Oracle, every D D L statement commits the open transaction, before and after it.
So an insert still waiting is made permanent as well, and a rollback cannot undo the D D L.
Every D D L statement is recorded in the data dictionary, which you can query like any other table.
User tables lists your tables. User tab columns lists their columns: member now has member name, and no fee.
Finally, DROP TABLE removes a table and all its rows. Another video compares DROP, TRUNCATE and DELETE.
Practise it in the SQL section of the course site.
